summary: Mineral County, MT tower on the Lolo NF: built 1934 as a 30-foot L-4, gone by 1967; no source describes what remains at the site today.

facts.design: L-4 observation cab on a 30-foot round timber tower
facts.status_note: Gone by 1967 per firelookout.com; no source says how or when it came down.

events.note: L-4 observation cab on a 30-foot round timber tower; construction reported from March 1934
Lloyd Reesman (early season) and Mabel Vann (late season) listed as lookouts
Firelookout.com says gone by 1967; the date and cause of removal are not in any source read

evidence.supports: about eight miles southeast of Superior
30-foot pole L-4 tower built in 1934, gone by 1967
evidence.quote: This 30' pole L-4 tower, built in 1934, was gone by 1967.
Known lookout personnel: 1950: Buddy Campbell; 1953: William Oliver; 1957: Lloyd Reesman (early season), Mabel Vann (late season).

evidence.supports: March 1934 crew constructing a lookout tower near Cobden
evidence.quote: A crew is constructing a lookout tower near Cobden, on the Lolo forest, to afford a better view of the timbered region in that vicinity for fire protection purposes.

evidence.supports: Lolo forest ordered materials for ten new lookout towers in 1934
evidence.quote: Materials for 10 new lookout towers and observatory building to be placed on the Lolo national forest this spring and summer have been ordered.

evidence.supports: one listed location was Cobden knob
L-4 observation cab built atop a 30-foot round timber tower in 1934
evidence.quote: 1934: An L-4 observation cab was built atop a 30-foot round timber tower.

evidence.supports: listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Both lookout write-ups agree on the 1934 build, the 30-foot L-4 design, the Lolo National Forest and the Mineral County location. Nothing in the sources read says how or when the tower came down beyond gone by 1967. A WebSearch surfaced an onXmaps trail listing (Cobden Point Lookout, FSR 9907) that says the tower was dismantled in 1967 and describes a route up Deep Creek Road (FSR 285). Fetching that page returned HTTP 404, so it is not cited anywhere. If it can be recovered, it would be the only source on the site today and would need a fresh quote check. The 'Removed' label on the Forest Lookouts page is not used as evidence.
